title.scientific: Global Biome Distribution: Climate, Altitude, and Latitude
title.algorithmic: Procedural Biome Generation using Height Maps and Perturbation Functions

scientific.concept: Biomes are large ecological communities characterized by vegetation types, climate, and fauna. Their global distribution is primarily determined by temperature and precipitation, following latitudinal and altitudinal patterns. The Holdridge and Köppen classification systems are fundamental frameworks.
scientific.analogy: Biomes are like floors in a climate skyscraper: the tropical floor (rainforest) is at the base where heat and moisture are abundant. As you 'ascend' in latitude or altitude, you pass through temperate forests, taigas, and finally tundra and ice at the 'rooftop'.
scientific.real_world_example: The Andes mountains show a dramatic vertical biome transition: from humid tropical forests at sea level, through cloud forests, páramos (high mountain grasslands), to Andean glaciers. This complete transition occurs in just 100 km of horizontal distance.
key_concepts: Biotemperature: mean temperature adjusted for biological limits (0-30°C)
Lapse rate: temperature decrease with altitude (~6.5°C per km)
Orographic precipitation: rain caused by forced ascent over mountains
Rain shadows: dry zones leeward of mountain ranges
Holdridge life zones: classification system based on biotemperature and precipitation
Isotherms: constant temperature lines that determine biome boundaries

algorithmic.algorithm: Biome assignment based on multiple influence maps: temperature, precipitation, altitude, using fuzzy state machines

complexity.time: O(n × b) where n is number of map pixels and b is number of biomes
complexity.space: O(n) to store the resulting biome map

algorithmic.why_this_algorithm: Fuzzy threshold assignment allows smooth transitions between biomes (ecotones) and captures natural variability. It's more efficient than complex ecological simulations while maintaining visual realism.

comparison.whittaker_plot: Whittaker diagram is simple but doesn't consider altitude
comparison.holdridge_hexagons: Holdridge is comprehensive but requires more parameters
comparison.machine_learning: ML can learn real patterns but needs large datasets
